page: UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 300 GB local SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2203.0 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 14.14 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression is highly efficient, reaching 39.49 GB/sec, which ranks in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 44425.64 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14883.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a cached read speed of 2685.2 GB/sec, which drops to 147.28 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, while write bandwidth is measured at 62.48 GB/sec.

The server exhibits a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose workloads, database operations, and web serving. Redis SET operations average 25.98 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 21.01 GB/sec. However, there is a notable performance tradeoff in text generation for small language models, which operates at a lower rate of 9.08 tokens per second. Given the shared CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance represents a cost-efficient option for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, and medium-scale database deployments that do not require dedicated CPU pinning or GPU acceleration.
